title: Arista di Maiale
subtitle: Florentine roast pork with rosemary and garlic
excerpt: A slow-roasted pork shoulder rubbed with garlic, rosemary and fennel seeds. The fat cap crisps as the meat cooks, basting itself throughout. This is Florentine Sunday lunch -- simple, unapologetic pork.
sourceNotes: Arista is the classic Florentine roast pork, cooked since the Renaissance. The name is said to come from Greek bishops at a council in Florence who called the dish 'aristos' -- the best. The recipe has barely changed.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze sliced leftovers in a little of the cooking juices for up to 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and marinate the pork the night before. Cook fresh on the day.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 160C / Gas 4. Start high at 220C for 20 minutes to crisp the skin.

content.text: Score the fat cap in a diamond pattern before rubbing with the paste. This allows the seasoning to penetrate and the fat to render more evenly. Start in a very hot oven and then reduce to finish slowly.

items.prepNote: bone-in or boneless, fat cap on
4 crushed to a paste for rubbing, 2 left whole for the tin
added to the tin during roasting
a generous amount -- especially over the fat

content.text: Score the fat cap in a diamond pattern about 1cm deep. Mix the garlic paste, rosemary, fennel seeds, olive oil, salt and pepper into a thick paste. Rub it all over the pork, pressing it into the cuts. Leave at room temperature for 1 hour, or refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 220C. Place the pork fat-side up in a roasting tin with the whole garlic cloves underneath. Roast for 20 minutes until the fat begins to crisp and colour.
Reduce the oven to 180C. Pour the wine into the bottom of the tin. Continue roasting for 1.5 to 2 hours, basting every 30 minutes. The internal temperature should reach 70C at the centre.
If the fat is not crisp enough, raise the oven to 220C for the final 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven. Rest uncovered for 20 minutes. This is not optional -- the juices need time to settle.
Carve and serve with the resting juices poured over. Roasted potatoes and a green salad are the traditional accompaniments.

items.symptom: Fat cap is soft and chewy, not crisp
items.cause: Oven not hot enough at the start, or pork not dried before cooking
items.fix: Pat the fat completely dry with kitchen paper before scoring. Start at 220C and do not rush the initial blast. A 10-minute blast at the end also helps.
Use a meat thermometer. Pull the pork at 70C. Let it rest fully covered loosely with foil for 20 minutes.

content.text: Arista is Sunday lunch in Tuscany. The Florentine version uses rosemary and fennel. In Umbria, black truffle is sometimes added to the paste. This version keeps it simple and traditional.
